title: Browser-ready SCOMP transport for Maintain client-server communication
description:
SCOMP should become the primary communication layer between browser clients and server runtimes for Maintain. Today, SCOMP transport support is strong for server-side/runtime-side usage, but browser compatibility is incomplete due to Node-specific dependencies in shared packages and transport implementations.

This epic delivers a production-usable browser-to-server path for request, signal, and feed semantics over WebSocket, while preserving existing server transports and wire protocol compatibility.
design: Add a browser-native transport package (e.g. @scomp/transport-websocket-browser) using globalThis.WebSocket. Remove/abstract Node-only runtime assumptions from shared types/protocol helpers (for example hash/crypto utilities currently tied to Node APIs). Keep server-side transport (@scomp/transport-websocket-server) and routing model unchanged where possible. Ensure metadata/auth/security context and priority hints continue to propagate end-to-end. Provide migration docs and a minimal browser+server example aligned with Maintain-style usage.
acceptance_criteria: Browser app can use @scomp/client + browser WebSocket transport without Node polyfills. Browser client can successfully execute request, signal, and feed flows against SCOMP server transport. Shared protocol/types compile and run in both browser and Node/Bun targets. Existing server transports (WebSocket server, RabbitMQ, in-process) remain compatible and pass tests. Integration tests cover success + failure cases (disconnect, timeout, unauthorized route, malformed payload). Documentation includes setup, route hints, security metadata handling, and a Maintain integration example.
